question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Study of sound and sound waves
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Acoustics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Acoustics" is the branch of science that deals with the study of sound and sound waves — their production, transmission, reception and effects. (ध्वनि-विज्ञान)

◦ Example: The acoustics of the new auditorium were tested before the concert.

• The word comes from the Greek "akoustikos" meaning "relating to hearing".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Botany" — the study of plants. (वनस्पति विज्ञान)

• Option 2 "Physics" — the general science of matter and energy; it is far too broad, not the specific study of sound.

• Option 3 "Demography" — the statistical study of human populations (births, deaths, migration). (जनसांख्यिकी)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes frequently asked in SSC exams:

◦ Ornithology — study of birds; Entomology — study of insects; Etymology — study of the origin of words.

◦ Seismology — study of earthquakes; Meteorology — study of weather; Numismatics — study of coins.

◦ Optics — study of light; Phonetics — study of speech sounds; Cardiology — study of the heart.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The students of class 7 gave their teacher a gift, which was ________ to her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. surprising.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A gift given by students to their teacher would be something unexpected and pleasant; the adjective that carries this positive sense of the unexpected is "surprising" (causing surprise/astonishment). (आश्चर्यजनक)

◦ Correct: The students of class 7 gave their teacher a gift, which was surprising to her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "revealing" means showing something previously hidden / giving away secret information — it does not fit a gift. (रहस्योद्घाटक)

• Option 2 "shocking" means causing horror, disgust or outrage — it carries a strongly negative connotation, unsuitable for a gift from students. (चौंका देने वाला/निंदनीय)

• Option 3 "confusing" means difficult to understand; bewildering — a gift is not normally described this way. (भ्रमित करने वाला)

NOTE

• Distinguish carefully between the "-ing" adjective (which describes the thing/cause) and the "-ed" adjective (which describes the person's feeling):

◦ The gift was surprising. / The teacher was surprised.

◦ The film was boring. / The audience was bored.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Obsession
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Fascination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obsession" means an idea or thought that continually preoccupies the mind; an overpowering, persistent interest in something. Its closest synonym among the options is "Fascination" (a very strong attraction or interest). (सनक / गहरी लगन)

◦ Example: His obsession/fascination with vintage cars made him spend all his savings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Discrimination" — unfair treatment of different categories of people; also the ability to judge finely. (भेदभाव)

• Option 3 "Unconcern" — a lack of interest or worry; this is the antonym of obsession. (उदासीनता)

• Option 4 "Sympathy" — feelings of pity and sorrow for someone's misfortune. (सहानुभूति)

NOTE

• Synonyms of obsession: fixation, mania, preoccupation, compulsion, infatuation, passion.

• Antonyms of obsession: indifference, unconcern, apathy, disinterest.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error and select the option which rectifies that error.

A lot of adulterants / are chemicals that can lead / to an range of health problems / in both children and adults.
option_1: to a range of health problems
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. to a range of health problems.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the third segment — "to an range of health problems". The article "an" is used only before a word beginning with a vowel sound. "Range" begins with the consonant sound /r/, so the correct article is "a".

◦ Correct: A lot of adulterants are chemicals that can lead to a range of health problems in both children and adults.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "are chemical that can lead" is wrong — the plural subject "a lot of adulterants" needs the plural noun "chemicals".

• Option 3 "A lot of adulterant" is wrong — "a lot of" with a countable noun takes the plural form "adulterants".

• Option 4 "in both children and adult." is wrong — "both ... and" here joins two plural nouns, so "adults" is required.

NOTE

• Article rule: a before a consonant sound (a university, a one-rupee coin, a European) and an before a vowel sound (an hour, an honest man, an MP, an umbrella).

• It is the sound, not the letter, that decides the article.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They would find someone drive the wagon back across the desert.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to drive the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment is "drive the". The sentence needs an infinitive of purpose after "find someone" — i.e. they would find a person whose job it would be to drive the wagon. Hence "someone to drive the wagon".

◦ Correct: They would find someone to drive the wagon back across the desert.

• Structure: find/get/need + someone + to + V1 (to-infinitive expressing purpose or the role of that person).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in drive in the" is grammatically meaningless — a preposition cannot be followed by the bare verb "drive".

• Option 2 "to drive" would delete the article "the", giving "someone to drive wagon back", which leaves the countable noun "wagon" without a determiner.

• Option 4 "in driving" removes the article as well and turns the purpose-infinitive into a gerund phrase that does not fit after "find someone".

NOTE

• Compare: "I need a man to repair the roof." / "She hired a tutor to teach the children."

• "Find someone doing something" (participle) means to discover a person in the act of doing it — a different meaning from the intended one here.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The ball / I kicked / went highly / in the sky.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. went highly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is in "went highly". Here the adverb must express physical height/distance, and the correct word for that is "high", not "highly".

◦ Correct: The ball I kicked went high in the sky.

• "High" = far up in physical position. "Highly" = very much / to a great degree (used with abstract meaning), e.g. "a highly qualified engineer", "she is highly respected".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "The ball" and Option 4 "I kicked" together form a correct contact/omitted relative clause — "The ball (which/that) I kicked".

• Option 3 "in the sky" is the correct prepositional phrase.

NOTE

• Other adverb pairs with the same trap:

◦ hard (with effort — "work hard") vs hardly (scarcely — "hardly any money").

◦ late (not on time) vs lately (recently).

◦ near (close by) vs nearly (almost).

◦ deep (far down) vs deeply (intensely, emotionally).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Rajat is known for his notorious nature. He will be friendly to your face but likes ____________.
option_2: to stab you in the back
option_3: to paint the whole town red
option_4: to get all bent out of the shape
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to stab you in the back.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to stab someone in the back" means to betray someone who trusts you; to harm a person secretly while pretending to be friendly. (पीठ पीछे धोखा देना)

◦ It fits perfectly with "friendly to your face but ..." — a clear contrast between outward friendliness and secret betrayal.

◦ Correct: He will be friendly to your face but likes to stab you in the back.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to blow one's own trumpet" — to praise oneself; to boast. (अपनी तारीफ़ खुद करना)

• Option 3 "to paint the town red" — to go out and celebrate wildly and noisily. (धूम मचाना)

• Option 4 "to get bent out of shape" — to become annoyed, upset or offended over something small. (नाराज़ हो जाना)

NOTE

• Related idioms of betrayal/two-facedness: "a wolf in sheep's clothing", "to double-cross someone", "to play both sides", "two-faced".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Barking up the wrong tree
option_2: To make a bad situation worse
option_3: Getting a good start is important
option_4: To be mistaken, to be looking for solutions in the wrong place
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To be mistaken, to be looking for solutions in the wrong place.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "barking up the wrong tree" means to pursue a mistaken line of thought or action; to accuse or blame the wrong person; to look for something in the wrong place. (ग़लत जगह प्रयास करना / ग़लत अनुमान लगाना)

◦ Example: If you think I broke the window, you are barking up the wrong tree — I was not even at home.

• Origin: it comes from hunting, where dogs would bark at the base of a tree believing the prey had climbed it, when in fact the animal had escaped up another tree.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Provoke trouble" corresponds to idioms like "stir up a hornet's nest" or "poke the bear".

• Option 2 "To make a bad situation worse" corresponds to "add fuel to the fire" or "rub salt into the wound".

• Option 3 "Getting a good start is important" corresponds to "well begun is half done" or "the early bird catches the worm".

NOTE

• Similar idioms of error/mistake: "to be on the wrong track", "to get hold of the wrong end of the stick", "to be off the mark".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A creature which depends on others
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Parasite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Parasite" is an organism that lives on or in another organism (the host) and depends on it for food and shelter, usually harming the host. Figuratively, it also means a person who lives off others without contributing. (परजीवी)

◦ Example: The tapeworm is a parasite that lives in the intestines of animals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Microbes" — a general term for microscopic organisms (bacteria, fungi, protozoa, viruses); it does not specifically mean "dependent on others". (सूक्ष्मजीव)

• Option 2 "Virus" — a submicroscopic infectious agent; although it needs a host cell to replicate, the exact one-word substitute for "a creature which depends on others" is *parasite*. (विषाणु)

• Option 4 "Bacteria" — single-celled microorganisms, many of which are free-living and even beneficial. (जीवाणु)

NOTE

• Related biology terms: Host — the organism on which a parasite lives; Symbiosis — a relationship in which both partners benefit; Saprophyte — an organism that feeds on dead and decaying matter; Autotroph — an organism that makes its own food.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

The play I saw last night was a ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. smash hit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "smash hit" means a very great success, especially a film, play, song or show that is extremely popular. (ज़बरदस्त सफलता)

◦ Correct: The play I saw last night was a smash hit.

• Grammatically too, the blank follows the article "a", so a noun phrase is required — only "smash hit" is a noun phrase; the other three are verb phrases.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hit the road" — to leave; to begin a journey. (निकल पड़ना)

• Option 2 "hit the hay/sack" — to go to bed; to go to sleep. (सोने जाना)

• Option 4 "hit the roof/ceiling" — to become extremely angry. (आपे से बाहर हो जाना)

NOTE

• Similar expressions for great success: "box-office hit", "blockbuster", "runaway success", "a roaring success".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He is _________ of many chain snatching cases in Dariyaganj.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. accused.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The only correctly spelt option is "accused" — spelt A-C-C-U-S-E-D (double "c", then "used").

• "To be accused of something" means to be charged with or blamed for an offence. (आरोपित होना)

◦ Correct: He is accused of many chain snatching cases in Dariyaganj.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "ackused", 2 "acxused" and 3 "akused" are all misspellings and have no meaning in English.

• Note the fixed preposition: accused of (not "accused for"). e.g. "He was accused of theft."

NOTE

• Related legal vocabulary: accuse (to charge), acquit (to declare not guilty), convict (to declare guilty), allege (to claim without proof), indict (to formally charge).

• Words with a double "c" that are commonly misspelt: accommodate, accessory, accelerate, occurrence, successful.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Despite the setbacks and obstacles we faced, / our team rallied together and achieved our goals, / which teach us the importance of / teamwork, resilience, and determination.
option_1: Despite the setbacks and obstacles we faced,
option_3: which teach us the importance of
option_4: our team rallied together and achieved our goals,
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. which teach us the importance of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relative pronoun "which" here refers back to the whole preceding idea (the team's rallying together and achieving its goals), which is treated as a singular notion; besides, the rest of the sentence is in the past tense.

◦ Correct: ... our team rallied together and achieved our goals, which taught us the importance of teamwork, resilience, and determination.

• Thus the present-tense plural verb "teach" is wrong — it should be "taught" (or "which teaches").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Despite the setbacks and obstacles we faced," is correct — "despite" is correctly followed by a noun phrase (not "despite of").

• Option 2 "teamwork, resilience, and determination" is a correct parallel list of nouns.

• Option 4 "our team rallied together and achieved our goals," is correct — both verbs are in the past tense.

NOTE

• Tense consistency: within one sentence, keep the verbs in the same time frame unless there is a logical reason to shift.

• "Which" referring to an entire clause takes a singular verb: "He failed the test, which was disappointing.".

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the spelling error that is underlined.

The questionaire used by the researcher was of top quality.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. questionnaire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "questionnaire" — Q-U-E-S-T-I-O-N-N-A-I-R-E (one "s", double "n", single "r", ending "-aire").

• A "questionnaire" is a set of printed questions used to collect information from people, especially for a survey or research. (प्रश्नावली)

◦ Correct: The questionnaire used by the researcher was of top quality.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quesstionnaire" wrongly doubles the "s".

• Option 3 "questionnairre" wrongly doubles the "r".

• Option 4 "questionnairee" wrongly doubles the final "e".

• The printed word in the sentence, "questionaire", is wrong because it has only a single "n".

NOTE

• The word comes from French; other "-aire" words: millionaire, commissionaire, doctrinaire, solitaire.

• Frequently misspelt research vocabulary: hypothesis, bibliography, questionnaire, phenomenon, analysis.

question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

That career competition was the difficultest exam he had ever given.
option_1: That career competition was the difficultest exam than any he had ever given.
option_2: That career competition was the most difficult exam than any he had ever given.
option_3: That career competition was the most difficultest exam he had ever given.
option_4: That career competition was the most difficult exam he had ever given.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. That career competition was the most difficult exam he had ever given.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Difficult" is a three-syllable (long) adjective. Long adjectives do not take the "-er/-est" endings; they form degrees with "more" and "the most".

◦ difficult – more difficult – the most difficult.

• Hence "the difficultest" is wrong and must be replaced by "the most difficult".

◦ Correct: That career competition was the most difficult exam he had ever given.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the wrong form "difficultest" and adds "than any", so it is doubly wrong.

• Option 2 wrongly mixes the superlative "the most difficult" with "than any"; the superlative is not used with "than".

• Option 3 "the most difficultest" is a double superlative — always incorrect.

NOTE

• Superlative with "ever" normally uses the pattern: the + superlative + (that) + subject + has/had ever + V3 — "the best film I have ever seen".

• Never combine "more/most" with "-er/-est": *more better, most easiest, worst-est* are all wrong.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the following sentence.

Shweta organises the sale of handmade pottery at a cheap rate.
option_3: Having one’s cake and eating it too
option_4: Making a fuss out of something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Go for a song.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "go for a song" means to be sold very cheaply / at a price far below the real value. (बहुत सस्ते में बिकना)

◦ Example: The antique furniture went for a song at the auction.

• It exactly matches "sale of handmade pottery at a cheap rate".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Hush money" — money paid to someone to keep a scandal or crime secret. (मुँह बंद रखने की रिश्वत)

• Option 3 "Have one's cake and eat it too" — to enjoy two desirable but mutually exclusive things at the same time. (दोनों हाथों में लड्डू)

• Option 4 "Make a fuss" — to show unnecessary excitement, worry or anger about something trivial. (छोटी बात पर हंगामा करना)

NOTE

• Related money idioms: "dirt cheap" (extremely cheap), "cost a fortune / an arm and a leg" (very expensive), "a steal" (a bargain), "at a throwaway price".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Guilty
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Innocent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Guilty" means responsible for a crime or wrongdoing; culpable. (दोषी)

• Its exact antonym is "Innocent" — not guilty of a crime or offence; blameless. (निर्दोष)

◦ Example: The court declared him innocent of all charges, so he was not guilty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Responsible" (accountable, answerable) is close in sense to "guilty" here, so it is a synonym-type distractor, not an antonym. (जिम्मेदार)

• Option 3 "Criminal" (one who has committed a crime) is also a synonym-type word. (अपराधी)

• Option 4 "Patient" (able to endure delay calmly) is completely unrelated. (धैर्यवान)

NOTE

• Synonyms of guilty: culpable, blameworthy, at fault, convicted, remorseful.

• Synonyms of innocent: blameless, faultless, guiltless, not guilty, naive.

• Legal note: in Indian law an accused is "presumed innocent until proven guilty".

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.

The colours of the rainbow seemed to shine through the trianguler prism as the sun hit the object.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. triangular.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence the incorrectly spelt word is "trianguler". Its correct spelling is "triangular" — T-R-I-A-N-G-U-L-A-R (the suffix is "-ar", not "-er").

• "Triangular" means shaped like a triangle; having three angles. (त्रिकोणीय)

◦ Correct: The colours of the rainbow seemed to shine through the triangular prism as the sun hit the object.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "rainbouw", 2 "son" and 4 "objact" are themselves misspellings of the correctly printed words in the sentence — "rainbow", "sun" and "object". They are distractors: those three words are already spelt correctly in the sentence.

NOTE

• Adjectives ending in "-ular": triangular, rectangular, circular, muscular, popular, particular, spectacular, molecular.

• A prism splits white light into its seven constituent colours — this is called dispersion (VIBGYOR).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The intrepid group of adventurers climbed the mountain despite of bad weather and road closures.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. despite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Despite" is a preposition meaning "in spite of"; it is never followed by "of". The underlined "despite of" is therefore wrong and must simply be "despite".

◦ Correct: The intrepid group of adventurers climbed the mountain despite bad weather and road closures.

• The parallel expression is "in spite of" (with "of"): "... in spite of bad weather".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "in spite" is incomplete — it must be "in spite of".

• Option 3 "in view of" means "considering / because of", which reverses the intended contrast.

• Option 4 "due to" indicates cause, not contrast; the sentence needs a contrast (they climbed *even though* the weather was bad).

NOTE

• Remember: despite + noun/gerund (no "of"); in spite of + noun/gerund; although/though/even though + clause (subject + verb).

◦ Despite the rain, we went out. / In spite of the rain, we went out. / Although it rained, we went out.

• "Intrepid" means fearless, bold and adventurous. (निडर)

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The airplane flowed over the mountains, offering the passengers a breath-taking view of the majestic peaks below.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. flew over.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb needed for an aeroplane is "fly", whose past tense is "flew" (fly – flew – flown). "Flowed" is the past tense of "flow", which is used for liquids (water, rivers, blood), not aircraft.

• The preposition "over" correctly expresses movement across and above the mountains, which explains the view of the peaks below.

◦ Correct: The airplane flew over the mountains, offering the passengers a breath-taking view of the majestic peaks below.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flew beyond" changes the meaning to "flew past/further than the mountains", which contradicts "the peaks below".

• Options 3 "flowed above" and 4 "flowed beyond" retain the wrong verb "flowed".

NOTE

• Verb forms: fly – flew – flown; flow – flowed – flowed.

• "Over" = directly above and across; "above" = at a higher level (not necessarily crossing); "beyond" = on the far side of.

• "Breath-taking" means astonishingly beautiful or impressive. (लुभावना)

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Ecstasy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Despair.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ecstasy" means an overwhelming feeling of great happiness or joyful excitement; rapture. (परमानंद)

• Its antonym is "Despair" — the complete loss or absence of hope; deep dejection. (निराशा)

◦ Example: Her ecstasy at winning turned to despair when the result was cancelled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Euphoria" (intense excitement and happiness) is a synonym of ecstasy, not an antonym. (उल्लास)

• Option 2 "Coarse" (rough in texture; rude/vulgar) is unrelated. (खुरदुरा / असभ्य)

• Option 3 "Natural" (existing in nature; normal) is unrelated. (प्राकृतिक)

NOTE

• Synonyms of ecstasy: rapture, bliss, elation, euphoria, delight, jubilation.

• Synonyms of despair: hopelessness, desolation, gloom, dejection, despondency.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As a boy, I was always exploring lonely places—neglected gardens and orchards, unoccupied houses, patches of scrub or wasteland, the fields outside the town, the fringes of the forest. On one of my rambles (1)________the bungalow, I pushed my way through a thicket of lantana bushes and stumbled over a thick stone slab, twisting my ankle slightly as I fell. For some time, I sat on the grass massaging my foot. When the pain eased, I looked more (2)________ at the stone slab and was surprised to find that it was a gravestone. It was almost entirely covered by ivy; obviously no one had been near it for years. I tugged at the ivy and some of it came away in my hands. There was some (3)________ lettering on the grave, half-obscured by grass and moss. I could make out a name—Rose—but little more. I sat there for some time, (4)________ over my discovery. I was wondering why ‘Rose’ should have been buried at so lonely a spot when there was a (5)________ not far away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. behind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a preposition of place describing where the boy was rambling: "on one of my rambles behind the bungalow". The overgrown, neglected patch with lantana bushes and a forgotten gravestone is naturally the rear/back area of the bungalow.

◦ Correct: On one of my rambles behind the bungalow, I pushed my way through a thicket of lantana bushes ...

• "Behind" means at the back of. (के पीछे)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "before" means "in front of / earlier than"; a neglected thicket with an old grave would not be in front of the house, and the time sense does not fit either.

• Option 3 "by dint of" means "by means of / because of" (e.g. "by dint of hard work") — it cannot follow "rambles" to indicate a place.

• Option 4 "below" means "under/lower than", which is impossible for rambles around a bungalow.

NOTE

• Prepositions of place commonly tested: behind (at the back of), beside (next to), between (two things), among (more than two), beneath/below (under), beyond (farther than).

• The passage is from Ruskin Bond's writing style of nostalgic boyhood exploration.

The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. closely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The narrator inspects the slab carefully and only then discovers that it is a gravestone; so he "looked more closely at the stone slab".

• "Closely" means carefully, attentively, in detail. (ध्यान से / बारीकी से)

◦ Correct: When the pain eased, I looked more closely at the stone slab and was surprised to find that it was a gravestone.

• The comparative "more" naturally collocates with "closely" — "look more closely" is a standard collocation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "emptily" means "in a vacant/blank manner" — it contradicts the careful observation that leads to a discovery.

• Option 3 "frankly" means "honestly, openly (in speech)" — it modifies speaking, not looking.

• Option 4 "lawfully" means "in accordance with the law" — completely irrelevant here.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "look": look closely / carefully / intently / keenly (attentively); look blankly / vacantly (without understanding).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As a boy, I was always exploring lonely places—neglected gardens and orchards, unoccupied houses, patches of scrub or wasteland, the fields outside the town, the fringes of the forest. On one of my rambles (1)________the bungalow, I pushed my way through a thicket of lantana bushes and stumbled over a thick stone slab, twisting my ankle slightly as I fell. For some time, I sat on the grass massaging my foot. When the pain eased, I looked more (2)________ at the stone slab and was surprised to find that it was a gravestone. It was almost entirely covered by ivy; obviously no one had been near it for years. I tugged at the ivy and some of it came away in my hands. There was some (3)________ lettering on the grave, half-obscured by grass and moss. I could make out a name—Rose—but little more. I sat there for some time, (4)________ over my discovery. I was wondering why ‘Rose’ should have been buried at so lonely a spot when there was a (5)________ not far away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. blurred.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The lettering on the old grave is "half-obscured by grass and moss" and the narrator "could make out a name—Rose—but little more". This shows the writing was faint and unclear, i.e. "blurred". (धुंधला)

◦ Correct: There was some blurred lettering on the grave, half-obscured by grass and moss.

• "Blurred" means indistinct, hazy, not clearly visible.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "idiotic" means extremely stupid — it cannot describe lettering. (मूर्खतापूर्ण)

• Option 2 "sturdy" means strong and solidly built — it describes physical strength, not visibility, and contradicts "half-obscured". (मज़बूत)

• Option 4 "nomadic" means wandering from place to place — irrelevant to lettering. (घुमंतू)

NOTE

• Synonyms of blurred: faint, indistinct, hazy, smudged, illegible, faded.

• Antonyms: clear, sharp, distinct, legible.

• Context clue technique: always read the words after the blank ("half-obscured by grass and moss") — they usually confirm the answer.

question: The Gua and Noamundi mines are located in with state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gua and Noamundi are famous iron ore mines located in the West Singhbhum district of Jharkhand, in the Singhbhum–Noamundi belt of the Chotanagpur plateau. (झारखंड)

◦ Noamundi mine is operated by Tata Steel and is one of the oldest mechanised iron ore mines in India (working since 1925).

◦ Gua mine is operated by the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jharkhand is India's leading producer of iron ore, coal and mica and is often called the "mineral bowl / Ruhr of India".

• Other important mineral areas of Jharkhand: Jharia and Bokaro (coal), Hazaribagh and Koderma (mica), Ghatshila (copper), Rajmahal (basalt).

• India's major iron-ore belts: Odisha–Jharkhand belt (Badampahar, Gua, Noamundi, Kiriburu), Durg–Bastar–Chandrapur belt (Bailadila, Dalli-Rajhara), Ballari–Chitradurga–Tumakuru belt (Kudremukh), and the Maharashtra–Goa belt.

NOTE

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (birth anniversary of Birsa Munda); its capital is Ranchi.

question: What is a fiscal year?
option_1: A year that represents the financial reporting period for the government
option_2: A year with a surplus in government revenue
option_3: A year with a deficit in government revenue
option_4: A year in which tax rates are increased
solution_text:
The correct answer is A year that represents the financial reporting period for the government.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "fiscal year" (also called the financial year) is the 12-month accounting period used by a government or a business for preparing budgets, accounts and financial statements. (वित्तीय वर्ष)

◦ In India, the fiscal year runs from 1 April to 31 March (e.g. FY 2023-24 = 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024).

◦ It has nothing to do with whether the year records a surplus, a deficit or a tax increase — those are outcomes, not definitions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 describes a revenue/budget surplus; Option 3 describes a deficit; Option 4 simply describes a tax change — none of these define a fiscal year.

• Assessment Year (AY), in Indian income-tax law, is the year following the previous (financial) year in which the income is assessed — income of FY 2023-24 is assessed in AY 2024-25.

• The Indian fiscal year of 1 April – 31 March was adopted in 1867, aligning India with the British government's accounting year.

NOTE

• Fiscal years elsewhere: USA — 1 October to 30 September; UK (government) — 1 April to 31 March; Japan — 1 April to 31 March; many countries (e.g. France, Germany) use the calendar year.

• Related terms: Fiscal deficit (total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings), Revenue deficit, Primary deficit (fiscal deficit minus interest payments).

question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, was passed in December 2022 and is related to which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed by Parliament in December 2022 and relates to Uttar Pradesh. (उत्तर प्रदेश)

◦ It moved the Gond community (along with its sub-groups Dhuria, Nayak, Ojha, Pathari and Rajgond) from the Scheduled Castes list to the Scheduled Tribes list in four districts of Uttar Pradesh — Chandauli, Kushinagar, Sant Kabir Nagar and Sant Ravidas Nagar (Bhadohi).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 341 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Castes of a state/UT, and Article 342 to specify the Scheduled Tribes; any change in these lists can be made only by an Act of Parliament.

• Around the same period Parliament also amended the SC/ST lists for Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka through separate Bills.

NOTE

• The first list of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was notified through the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.

• The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (Article 338) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338-A, created by the 89th Amendment, 2003) are the constitutional watchdogs.

question: Identify the Kuchipudi dancer from following, who was awarded with ‘Padma Shri’ in the year 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padmaja Reddy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Padmaja Reddy is a celebrated Kuchipudi exponent from Telangana who was conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 in the field of Art (Dance). (पद्मश्री 2022 — कुचिपुड़ी)

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village Kuchipudi (Kuchelapuram) in Krishna district.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Vidyanand Sarek — a poet and folk-song writer of Himachal Pradesh, Padma Shri 2022 for Literature and Education.

• Option 3 Dr. Veeraswamy Seshiah — a noted diabetologist from Tamil Nadu, Padma Shri 2022 for Medicine.

• Option 4 KV Rabiya — a social activist from Kerala known for her literacy campaign despite disability, Padma Shri 2022 for Social Work.

NOTE

• Kuchipudi features the Tarangam item (dancing on the rim of a brass plate balancing a pot of water); it was popularised by Siddhendra Yogi.

• Famous Kuchipudi dancers: Vempati Chinna Satyam, Raja & Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Shobha Naidu, Swapnasundari.

• India's civilian awards in order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri; they were instituted in 1954.

question: Buddha Purnima is marked on a full moon day in the Hindu month of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaisakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Buddha Purnima (also called Vesak or Buddha Jayanti) is celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) of the Hindu month of Vaisakh (April–May). (वैशाख पूर्णिमा)

• The day commemorates the triple event in the life of Gautama Buddha:

◦ his birth at Lumbini (Nepal),

◦ his enlightenment (Nirvana/Bodhi) at Bodh Gaya (Bihar),

◦ his Mahaparinirvana (death) at Kushinagar (Uttar Pradesh).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Buddha's first sermon — the Dharmachakra Pravartana — was delivered at Sarnath near Varanasi.

• The four noble truths (Arya Satya) and the Eightfold Path (Ashtangika Marga) form the core of his teaching; his teachings were originally preserved in the Pali language (the Tripitaka: Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma Pitaka).

NOTE

• Order of Hindu months: Chaitra, Vaisakh, Jyaistha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadra(pada), Ashwin, Kartik, Margashirsha, Pausha, Magha, Phalguna.

• Other important Purnimas: Guru Purnima (Ashadha), Raksha Bandhan (Shravana), Sharad Purnima (Ashwin), Kartik Purnima (Kartik, also Guru Nanak Jayanti), Holika Dahan (Phalguna).

question: Which of the following is the official language of Afghanistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Afghanistan has two official languages — Dari (Afghan Persian) and Pashto. Of the given options, only Dari is an official language of Afghanistan. (दरी — अफ़ग़ानिस्तान)

• Dari is a variety of Persian (Farsi) and serves as the country's principal lingua franca; Pashto is spoken mainly by the Pashtun population.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Sinhala — an official language of Sri Lanka (along with Tamil).

• Option 2 Burmese — the official language of Myanmar.

• Option 4 Dzongkha — the national language of Bhutan.

NOTE

• Afghanistan: capital Kabul; currency Afghan Afghani; it shares its eastern border with Pakistan along the Durand Line (1893).

• Afghanistan is a landlocked country bordered by Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and China (the narrow Wakhan Corridor).

• Other neighbours' languages: Nepal — Nepali; Bangladesh — Bengali; Maldives — Dhivehi; China — Mandarin.

question: Who started the temple entry movement in 1927?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimrao Ambedkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar launched the temple entry movement in 1927 to secure for the depressed classes the right to enter temples and to use public water sources. (डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर)

◦ In March 1927 he led the historic Mahad Satyagraha (Chavdar Tale Satyagraha) in Maharashtra to assert the right of untouchables to draw water from the public Chavdar tank.

◦ In 1930 he led the Kalaram Temple Satyagraha at Nashik, a landmark temple-entry agitation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 M. G. Ranade — a 19th-century social reformer, founder of the Prarthana Samaj and a founder of the Indian National Congress; he died in 1901.

• Option 3 Mahatma Gandhi — campaigned against untouchability and founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932), but the 1927 temple entry movement is credited to Ambedkar.

• Option 4 Annie Besant — Theosophist leader who started the Home Rule League (1916) and became the first woman President of the Congress (1917).

NOTE

• Ambedkar founded Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924), and the newspapers Mooknayak (1920) and Bahishkrit Bharat (1927).

• He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution and India's first Law Minister; he was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.

• The Poona Pact (1932) between Gandhi and Ambedkar replaced separate electorates with reserved seats for the depressed classes.

question: In which state is Gobind Sagar (Bhakra Nangal Project) located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gobind Sagar is the reservoir created by the Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej river, and it lies in the Bilaspur district of Himachal Pradesh. (हिमाचल प्रदेश)

• It is named after Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

• The Bhakra Nangal Project is a joint venture of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, administered by the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), but the Bhakra dam and its reservoir are physically situated in Himachal Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bhakra Dam is one of the highest gravity dams in the world (about 226 m); Jawaharlal Nehru called it "the new temple of resurgent India".

• The Nangal Dam lies downstream in Punjab, and the Nangal Hydel Channel feeds power houses and canals.

• The Sutlej (Satluj) rises from the Rakshastal lake near Mansarovar in Tibet and enters India through the Shipki La pass.

NOTE

• Other major river-valley projects: Hirakud (Mahanadi, Odisha), Nagarjuna Sagar (Krishna, Telangana/AP), Tehri (Bhagirathi, Uttarakhand), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada, Gujarat), Damodar Valley Corporation (Jharkhand/West Bengal).

question: Pandit Ravi Shankar is known worldwide for playing which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (1920–2012) was the world's most famous sitar maestro; he introduced Indian classical music to Western audiences through his association with George Harrison of the Beatles and performances at Woodstock and the Concert for Bangladesh. (सितार)

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (1999), the Padma Vibhushan (1981) and multiple Grammy Awards.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Mohan Veena — invented and popularised by Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt (Grammy winner).

• Option 2 Sarod — associated with Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan.

• Option 3 Been (Rudra Veena/Pungi) — the "been" is popularly linked with snake charmers and with the Rudra Veena tradition of Ustad Asad Ali Khan.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tata Vadya (stringed — sitar, sarod, veena, santoor), Sushira Vadya (wind — flute, shehnai), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam), Ghana Vadya (solid percussion — manjira, jaltarang).

• Other maestros: Bismillah Khan (shehnai), Hariprasad Chaurasia (flute), Zakir Hussain (tabla), Shivkumar Sharma (santoor), Anoushka Shankar (sitar, daughter of Ravi Shankar).

question: The Arabian Sea is an extension of which of the following oceans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian ocean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arabian Sea is a northern arm (extension) of the Indian Ocean, lying between the Indian peninsula on the east and the Arabian Peninsula (Horn of Africa) on the west. (अरब सागर — हिंद महासागर का विस्तार)

• Its important gulfs and inlets are the Gulf of Aden (connecting to the Red Sea through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait), the Gulf of Oman (connecting to the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz), the Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Bay of Bengal, also part of the Indian Ocean, lies to the east of the Indian peninsula; the two are joined south of India by the Indian Ocean proper, with the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar separating India from Sri Lanka.

• Rivers draining into the Arabian Sea: Indus, Narmada, Tapi, Mahi, Sabarmati and the west-flowing rivers of Kerala/Karnataka.

• The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean and the only one named after a country.

NOTE

• Order of oceans by size: Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic.

• India's coastline touches the Arabian Sea (west), the Bay of Bengal (east) and the Indian Ocean (south); Kanyakumari is the meeting point of the three water bodies.

question: Which of the following is a dimension of microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Outreach to rural areas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Microfinance institutions (MFIs) provide small-value loans and other financial services to low-income households and micro-enterprises that are excluded from formal banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान)

• One of the key dimensions used to measure the performance of MFIs is their "outreach" — how far and how deep they reach, especially into rural and underserved areas (number of clients, number of villages/branches covered, proportion of women and poor borrowers served).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are not defining dimensions of microfinance: interest rates are an operating variable, stock-market investment is not a microfinance activity at all, and credit cards belong to mainstream retail banking.

• Delivery models in India: the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP) launched by NABARD in 1992, and the Joint Liability Group (JLG) model used by NBFC-MFIs.

• The Malegam Committee (2011) recommended the creation of a separate category of NBFC-MFIs, which the RBI accepted.

NOTE

• Bandhan Bank began as a microfinance institution and later became a universal bank (2015).

• Globally, Prof. Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh won the Nobel Peace Prize (2006) for pioneering microcredit.

• Related Indian schemes: PM MUDRA Yojana (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun), Stand Up India, and SIDBI's microfinance refinancing.

question: Shambhu Maharaj was a renowned guru of which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lucknow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Shambhu Maharaj (1907–1970) was one of the greatest gurus of the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak. (लखनऊ घराना — कथक)

• He belonged to the illustrious family of Kalka–Bindadin; he was the son of Acchan Maharaj's father Kalka Prasad and the uncle of Pandit Birju Maharaj.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, and he headed the Kathak wing of Bharatiya Kala Kendra, Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Lucknow Gharana is noted for bhava (expression), grace and abhinaya, and it flourished under the patronage of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh.

• The Jaipur Gharana emphasises layakari (rhythmic virtuosity) and fast footwork; the Banaras Gharana was developed by Janakiprasad; the Raigarh Gharana was fostered by Raja Chakradhar Singh of Raigarh (Chhattisgarh).

NOTE

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India, derived from "Katha" (story) told by "Kathakars"; it is the only classical dance form with strong Persian/Mughal influence.

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which is the oldest Stupa of the Buddhist Period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanchi Stupa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh) is regarded as the oldest surviving stone structure/stupa in India, originally built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. (साँची स्तूप)

• It was later enlarged during the Shunga period and the famous four ornamented gateways (toranas) were added by the Satavahanas (1st century BCE).

• Sanchi was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Dhamek Stupa — at Sarnath (Varanasi), marking the spot of Buddha's first sermon; the present structure dates to the Gupta period (c. 500 CE).

• Option 2 Mahabodhi Temple — at Bodh Gaya (Bihar), the place of Buddha's enlightenment; a UNESCO site (2002).

• Option 3 Kesariya Stupa — in East Champaran, Bihar; it is the tallest Buddhist stupa in India (about 104 feet).

NOTE

• Parts of a stupa: Anda (hemispherical dome), Harmika (railing on top), Yashti/Chhatra (umbrella mast), Medhi (drum/base), Vedika (railing) and Pradakshina Patha (circumambulatory path).

• Sanchi's Lion Capital-style pillar and the Ashokan edicts also stand there; the Sarnath Lion Capital is India's State Emblem.

question: Who conducts elections for both the houses of Parliament in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Election Commission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Election Commission of India (ECI) conducts elections to both Houses of Parliament — the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha — as well as to the State Legislatures and to the offices of the President and Vice-President. (भारत निर्वाचन आयोग)

• It is a permanent, independent constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution, set up on 25 January 1950 (celebrated as National Voters' Day).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The ECI does not conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities — these are held by the State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA.

• Composition: originally a single-member body; since 1993 it has been a three-member body — the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners, deciding by majority.

• The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

• India's first CEC was Sukumar Sen.

NOTE

• Related articles: 324 (superintendence of elections), 325 (no exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex), 326 (adult suffrage — voting age reduced from 21 to 18 by the 61st Amendment, 1988).

question: The third battle of Panipat was fought in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1761.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Marathas, led by Sadashivrao Bhau (with Vishwasrao, son of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao), and the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani), supported by Najib-ud-Daula of Rohilkhand and Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh. (पानीपत का तृतीय युद्ध, 1761)

• The Marathas suffered a crushing defeat, which halted their northward expansion and indirectly helped the British rise to power in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• First Battle of Panipat (1526) — Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, founding the Mughal Empire; first major use of field artillery and the tulughma tactic in India.

• Second Battle of Panipat (1556) — Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan defeated Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya).

• 1707 is the year of the death of Aurangzeb; the Third Anglo-Mysore War treaty and other events fall around 1786/1792, but none relate to Panipat.

NOTE

• Panipat lies in present-day Haryana, on the historic route from the north-west into the Gangetic plains.

question: Which dance form is associated with Natwari Dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Natwari Nritya" is another name for Kathak, particularly the Braj/Banaras tradition associated with the dance of Lord Krishna (Krishna is called "Natwar"). (नटवरी नृत्य — कथक)

• It was revived in modern times by Pandit Gopi Krishna and the Banaras gharana; the term stresses Kathak's origin in the storytelling of Krishna's Raslila.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathak developed from the recitals of Kathakars (story-tellers) in temples of North India, and later flourished in the Mughal courts, absorbing Persian elements.

• Its three main gharanas are Lucknow (expression/bhava), Jaipur (layakari/footwork) and Banaras; the Raigarh gharana is a later offshoot.

• Distinctive features: tatkar (footwork), chakkars (spins), ghungroos (ankle bells), thaat, aamad, tora, tukra.

NOTE

• Option 2 Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; Option 3 Odissi — Odisha, marked by the tribhanga posture; Option 4 Kathakali — Kerala, famous for elaborate make-up (chutti) and costumes.

• Famous Kathak exponents: Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Gopi Krishna, Kumudini Lakhia.

question: The directive principles are largely classified into three broad categories. Which of the following is NOT the part of this classification?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Authoritative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution, are generally classified into three broad categories:

◦ Socialistic principles (e.g. Articles 38, 39, 41, 42, 43 — adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, right to work, living wage).

◦ Gandhian principles (e.g. Articles 40, 43, 43B, 46, 47, 48 — village panchayats, cottage industries, promotion of SC/ST interests, prohibition of intoxicating drinks, ban on cow slaughter).

◦ Liberal–Intellectual principles (e.g. Articles 44, 45, 48, 48A, 49, 50, 51 — uniform civil code, early childhood care, protection of environment and monuments, separation of judiciary from executive, promotion of international peace).

• "Authoritative" is not one of these categories.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• DPSPs are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland; they are non-justiciable (not enforceable in a court) but "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37).

• Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), 43A (workers' participation in management) and 48A (environment) were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976; Article 38(2) was added by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

NOTE

• Fundamental Rights (Part III) are justiciable, DPSPs (Part IV) are not; the Minerva Mills case (1980) held that a balance between the two is part of the basic structure.

• Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

question: Which soft metal in group 1 of the periodic table tarnishes within a few seconds of exposure to air?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sodium (Na) is a soft alkali metal of Group 1 which is so reactive that a freshly cut surface tarnishes within a few seconds on exposure to air, forming a layer of sodium oxide/hydroxide. (सोडियम)

◦ Reactions: 4Na + O₂ → 2Na₂O; 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ (with fire).

◦ Because of this reactivity, sodium (and potassium) is stored under kerosene oil.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 Barium (Ba) and 3 Strontium (Sr) belong to Group 2 (alkaline earth metals), not Group 1.

• Option 4 Francium (Fr) is a Group 1 element but it is extremely rare and radioactive, occurring only in trace amounts; it is not the metal referred to in ordinary laboratory observation.

• Group 1 (alkali metals): Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr — all soft, low-density metals with one valence electron, forming +1 ions.

NOTE

• Flame test colours: Na — golden yellow, K — lilac/violet, Li — crimson red, Ca — brick red, Sr — crimson, Ba — apple green, Cu — bluish green.

• Sodium compounds in daily life: NaCl (common salt), NaHCO₃ (baking soda), Na₂CO₃·10H₂O (washing soda), NaOH (caustic soda).

question: The ‘Ka Shad Mastieh’ or victory dance of the____________ tribe of Meghalaya is an ancient war dance performed during the prominent festival of the tribe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khasi.

• "Ka Shad Mastieh" is the ancient war/victory dance of the Khasi tribe of Meghalaya, performed to celebrate victory in battle and now presented during the tribe's prominent festivals. (खासी जनजाति — मेघालय)

• Male dancers carry a sword (waitlam) and a whisk/shield, symbolising valour and protection.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Meghalaya's three main tribes are the Khasi, Garo and Jaintia — collectively called the "hill tribes"; the Bhoi and War are sub-groups of the Khasi community.

• Other Khasi dances/festivals: Ka Shad Suk Mynsiem (dance of the joyful heart, spring festival), Ka Pomblang Nongkrem (Nongkrem dance, a five-day thanksgiving festival), Ka Shad Nongkrem.

• The Garos celebrate Wangala (the hundred-drums festival), and the Jaintias celebrate Behdienkhlam.

NOTE

• The Khasi, Garo and Jaintia societies are matrilineal — descent and property pass through the mother, and the youngest daughter (Ka Khadduh) inherits the ancestral property.

• Meghalaya, "the abode of clouds", became a full state on 21 January 1972; its capital is Shillong.

question: Which vitamin is needed for a healthy immune system, low-light vision, and healthy skin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin A (Retinol) is essential for a healthy immune system, for vision in dim/low light and for healthy skin and mucous membranes. (विटामिन A — रेटिनॉल)

◦ In the retina it combines with the protein opsin to form rhodopsin (visual purple), the pigment needed for night vision.

◦ Its deficiency causes night blindness (nyctalopia), xerophthalmia and Bitot's spots.

• Sources: carrot, papaya, mango, green leafy vegetables, milk, butter, egg yolk, cod-liver oil; plant sources supply beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Vitamin K (Phylloquinone) — needed for blood clotting; deficiency causes excessive bleeding.

• Option 2 Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) — deficiency causes cheilosis, glossitis and cracked lips.

• Option 3 Vitamin B9 (Folic acid) — needed for DNA synthesis and RBC formation; deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia and neural tube defects in newborns.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K (stored in the body); water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C (not stored, needed daily).

• Chemical names: A — Retinol, B1 — Thiamine, B3 — Niacin, B12 — Cyanocobalamin, C — Ascorbic acid, D — Calciferol, E — Tocopherol, K — Phylloquinone.
